_comment: Model preference order for the assist service. Tried strictly in order; first to answer wins.
Updated 2026-08-23 on <YOUR_NAME>'s instruction to make the nano-omni model primary.
NOTE ON THE NAME: the model is nemotron-3-nano-omni (not nemotron-2). Full id below.
MEASURED 2026-08-23, three runs each on a realistic prompt. JSON-envelope compliance is
what matters most here, because the citation guardrail in verify.mjs depends on it:
model                                              avg      JSON ok   note
nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning:free        3496ms   3/3       only reliable one
stealth/ox-alpha                                   2421ms   0/3       HTTP 429, rate limited
nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free                    5933ms   1/3       valid when not throttled
nemotron-3.5-lightning:free                        3132ms   0/3       leaks reasoning, never JSON
WHY NANO-OMNI IS PRIMARY, beyond raw speed: it is the only model of the four that produced
a parseable envelope on every run. stealth/ox-alpha LOOKS fastest by average, but its quick
runs (491ms, 444ms) were 429 rejections rather than answers — counting those as speed is a
measurement error. A model that fails fast still costs a full retry cycle downstream, so on
real drafts it is slower than the number suggests.
ORDER CHANGE BEYOND THE INSTRUCTION, flagged for review: stealth/ox-alpha was moved from
position 1 to 3 because it is currently rate-limited on this key and would waste a call on
most drafts. That was a judgement call in service of the stated goal (speed). To restore
the previous order, put stealth/ox-alpha back at the top — nothing else depends on it.
nemotron-3.5-lightning stays last: it reproducibly answers with "Here's a thinking process:"
instead of JSON, so it only ever costs a wasted call. Kept because <YOUR_NAME> listed it; drop
it freely.
fallbackToDiscovered: when every model below fails, fall back to live free-model discovery
rather than failing the request outright.

2026-09-11: stealth/ox-alpha removed (404, testing period ended) and nemotron-3.5-lightning removed (hangs past 45s, never JSON). Measured on the real reply prompt: nano-omni 24s valid JSON, ultra-550b hung.

2026-09-11: codex:gpt-5.6-sol is PRIMARY — <YOUR_NAME>'s ChatGPT/Codex subscription through the Codex CLI's own auth (~/.codex/auth.json, refreshed automatically). 2.8s per short reply. OpenRouter free models remain as fallback only.

2026-09-25: ChatGPT/Codex is being cancelled, so codex:gpt-5.6-sol is OUT of the preferred list (the codex: provider code in runner.mjs is untouched and still works if it is ever added back). claude:sonnet is now PRIMARY — <YOUR_NAME>'s Claude Max subscription via `claude -p`, run agentically with every configured tool and MCP server loaded, restricted at the CLI's own permission layer to a read-only allowlist (CLAUDE_READ_ALLOWLIST in runner.mjs); writes/sends are denied by --permission-mode dontAsk plus an explicit denylist. omniroute:hermes-fallback (Hermes' local OpenAI-compatible gateway) is second, ahead of the OpenRouter free-tier fallbacks below.
